exposure: antenatal corticosteroid administration-to-birth interval (no antenatal corticosteroids)
antenatal corticosteroid administration-to-birth interval (partial antenatal corticosteroids: less than 24 hours before birth)
antenatal corticosteroid administration-to-birth interval (1-7 days before birth)
antenatal corticosteroid administration-to-birth interval (greater than 7 days before birth)
outcome: composite adverse outcome (neonatal mortality, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, grade 3-4 intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular leukomalacia, or stage 3 or higher retinopathy)
cohort: The study included 6,870 singleton neonates born between 24 0/7 and 33 6/7 weeks of gestation who were admitted to tertiary neonatal units in Canada during 2010-2012.
finding: Antenatal corticosteroids provided maximum benefit in reducing adverse neonatal outcomes when administered between 1 and 7 days before birth.
